title: Former Liang
capsule: Former Liang (前涼, Qián Liáng) was a Han Chinese state ruling the Hexi Corridor and adjacent Western Regions from its capital at Guzang (modern Wuwei, Gansu), one of the Sixteen Kingdoms that emerged from the fragmentation of the Western Jin dynasty. The Zhang family, beginning with Zhang Gui around 301, governed the state as nominal vassals of the Eastern Jin court; the dynasty reached its political and cultural apex under Zhang Jun (324–346), who extended control over oasis cities deep into Central Asia and made Guzang a refuge for Jin literati, earning the region a reputation as a custodian of Han culture. Former Liang survived largely through diplomatic flexibility and geographic isolation until Former Qin under Fu Jiān invaded in 376, compelling the last ruler Zhang Tianxi to surrender—ending 75 years of autonomous Zhang rule.
